lesson.title: Apps, permissions and AI tools in class
lesson.subtitle: Check it first, allow only what it needs, keep pupils anonymous

video.title: Apps, permissions and AI tools in class
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds; narration in the lesson language, captions as separate files.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — university lecturer in education (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: A quiz that wants your contacts

scenes.visual: Farah looks at a colourful quiz app on her phone; three permission pop-ups stack up: location, contacts, microphone.
scenes.animation: Pop-ups stack one on top of the other.
scenes.narration: A colleague showed me a free quiz app last week. The pupils loved it. Then I read what it asks for: their location, their contacts and the microphone. For a quiz?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the course name.
scenes.on_screen_text: Apps, permissions and AI tools in class
scenes.narration: Today: how to check an app or an AI tool before you use it with a class.

scenes.visual: A checklist of four questions beside a phone.
scenes.animation: Each question ticks in as it is asked.
scenes.narration: Before you use any app with pupils, ask four questions. Who makes it? What data does it take? How old must users be? And what can you switch off in its settings?

scenes.visual: Four cards: an age badge, a parent, a coin, a school building.
scenes.animation: Cards flip in one by one.
scenes.narration: Many apps and chatbots set a minimum age, often thirteen. Younger teens usually need a parent’s permission. A free app has to pay for itself somehow, and often that’s with data. So sign pupils up with school accounts, never their personal phone numbers.

scenes.visual: A phone’s permission screen with switches for camera, microphone, contacts and location.
scenes.animation: Switches flip off, one stays on.
scenes.narration: A permission is an app asking to use part of your phone: the camera, the microphone, your contacts or your location. Allow only what the app really needs to do its job. Choose “only while using the app”, and approximate location when you can.

scenes.visual: A plumber at the school door; the caretaker gives him the tap room key, not the office keys.
scenes.animation: One key passes hands; the office door stays shut.
scenes.narration: It’s like a plumber visiting the school. He needs the tap, not the office keys or the staff register. You give each visitor only the rooms their job needs.

scenes.visual: Mr Joseph holds up a phone with the quiz app’s three requests. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A free quiz app asks for location, contacts and the microphone. It only shows quiz questions. What do you allow?

scenes.visual: All three switches go off; the quiz still loads with a check badge.
scenes.animation: Switches click off; the quiz page appears.
scenes.narration: None of them. A quiz needs none of those to work, and you can say no and still use it. If an app won’t work without permissions it doesn’t need, choose another app.

scenes.visual: A chatbot window. On the left, red cards it should never see; on the right, green safer ways.
scenes.animation: Red cards bounce off the chat box; green ones go in.
scenes.narration: AI chatbots need extra care. Never paste pupils’ names, marks, health or behaviour notes into one. Write “Pupil A” instead, and change any detail that could identify a child. Check its settings too: many let you stop your chats being used to train the AI.

scenes.visual: A staff-room computer and a cyber café booth, each with a sign-out button highlighted.
scenes.narration: Shared computers need care too, in the staff room or a cyber café. Use a private window. Never tick “remember me”. And always sign out before you leave.

scenes.visual: Four app icons ask for permissions; a hand allows one switch per app.
scenes.animation: Switches flip as the hand moves.
scenes.narration: In the lab, four new apps ask for permissions. Allow only what each one really needs, and learn the warning signs.

scenes.visual: Farah reads over a colleague’s shoulder: a chatbot window with a pupil’s full name and medical notes. Two answer cards bounce in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A teacher asks an AI tool to help write a report on a pupil, and pastes in the pupil’s full name and medical notes. Safe, or not safe?

scenes.animation: Cards line up left to right.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check · Allow less · Anonymous · Sign out
scenes.narration: Not safe: health details are sensitive, so leave out the name and the medical notes. Remember: ask four questions first, allow only what an app needs, keep pupils anonymous in AI tools, and sign out of shared computers.

scenes.visual: Farah’s classroom. Four app icons drawn on the board; pupils vote with thumbs up or down for each permission.
scenes.animation: Ticks and crosses appear beside each app.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: draw four apps on the board, a torch, a map, a quiz and a camera. Pupils decide which permissions each one really needs, and explain why.

checkpoints.prompt: A free quiz app asks for location, contacts and the microphone. It only shows quiz questions. What do you allow?

options.text: All three — the app is free
None of them — the quiz still works

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a quiz needs none of those. Say no, and it still works.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a quiz needs no location, contacts or microphone. Deny all three; if it won’t work, choose another app.

checkpoints.prompt: A teacher pastes a pupil’s full name and medical notes into an AI tool to help write a report. Safe or not safe?

options.text: Safe — the AI keeps it private
Not safe — leave out the name and health details

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — health details are sensitive. Use “Pupil A” and leave out anything that identifies the child.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — what you paste leaves your hands and may be stored. Use “Pupil A” and no health details.
